text:
Two of the best young stories in the league share the ice in Anaheim. Matthew Schaefer, the Islanders' 19-year-old defenseman, has 11 points in his last ten games and a four-game point streak, and NHL.com spent the week listing the Hall of Famers he keeps catching on the teenage-defenseman charts (Bobby Orr and Scott Stevens among them). Cutter Gauthier keeps scoring: TSN asked this week where he ranks among the NHL's elite goal scorers, and our numbers have him at 47% to score tonight, the highest of anyone in this game.

The Islanders snapped a four-game winless run with a 5-2 win in Los Angeles on Thursday, and their season comes with a warning label. They're plus-1 in goal difference on chances worth minus-10.5, and goaltending is doing the lifting: 12.2 goals saved above expected, 9.4 of them by Ilya Sorokin, tonight's projected starter. Bo Horvat plays his 900th game, and rookie Victor Eklund has goals in four straight, a few days after Mason Marchment was fined the maximum for roughing him. Calum Ritchie and Alexander Romanov are out; Jean-Gabriel Pageau is day to day.

Anaheim's five-game winning streak ended with a 4-2 loss to Nashville on Wednesday. Like the Islanders, the Ducks have been outchanced more often than not (45% of the expected goals at five on five), and their scoring (3.74 goals a game) has outrun the chances. Ryan Poehling is out with a knee injury until December, so Judd Caulfield has moved up beside Nikita Nesterenko and Alex Killorn, and Gauthier's ice time is up to 19:22 a night. Laurent Brossoit had won four straight before Wednesday, but Lukas Dostal is our projected starter, 1.3 goals worse than expected this season.

The special teams are the matchup to watch: Anaheim's power play creates 0.77 expected goals a game, the Islanders' penalty kill allows 0.90, and the Ducks take 5.1 penalties a game themselves. Our numbers have it close, 3.30 expected goals for Anaheim to 3.08. They met on Oct. 20, a 3-2 Islanders win they deserved 88% of the time.
headline: Schaefer and Gauthier meet in Anaheim
